The panel is a real patient image showing a large bladder diverticulum with a gas–fluid level, which maps to gas within the bladder/diverticulum lumen. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial abdominal CT of a human patient showing gas within the bladder lumen and mural gas with bladder wall thickening, matching the caption and the diagnosis of emphysematous cystitis stated in the article. B: Coronal CT reconstruction of the same patient showing bladder gas and wall gas plus extension of air intra- and retroperitoneally, consistent with the captioned diagnosis of emphysematous cystitis with extravesical gas spread.

panels.figure_caption: Computed tomography scan of the abdomen showed air in the bladder and the thickened bladder wall, associated with air intra- and retroperitoneally.
in_text_mentions: Despite painkillers, the patient continued complaining of abdominal pain. Because of the severity of his pain, computed tomography scan of the abdomen was performed. This revealed air in the bladder and the thickened bladder wall, associated with air intra- and retroperitoneally. Furthermore, bilateral pleural fluid, some free fluid in the peritoneal cavity, and a few dilated jejunal segments without characteristics of bowel ischemia were seen (Figures 1(a) and 1(b)). The diagnosis of emphysematous cystitis was made.
